project.name: Kingsbarns
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 10 of 13: every visitor category, strict boundary, all four named trail providers, local HES/NRHE completeness, construction dates, access, transport and dogs were rechecked before continuing. Kingsbarns Distillery, Cambo Gardens and Kingsbarns Golf Links remain separate attractions. Their customer facilities do not inflate the village score.

touristAppeal.label: Worth a Visit
touristAppeal.summary: Kingsbarns remains a genuine 72-point visit: the historic village has a qualifying daytime inn and five usable route downloads, while the named walkable beach cluster adds a strong shore, seasonal food, picnic space, public parking and toilets. Cambo, the distillery and golf remain separate.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The beach and walking routes are strong outdoor choices and the Inn explicitly welcomes dogs in the bar; wildlife, livestock, roads, golf and the unconfirmed food-truck policy still require close control and planning.

visitorHighlights.name: Kingsbarns Beach (Cambo Sands)
visitorHighlights.reason: A two-mile award-winning shore with dunes, wildlife, coastal walking and a complete managed visitor cluster behind the beach.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Two miles of dunes and wildlife
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air beach; daylight visit recommended. Managed car park and an overnight toilet are available year-round.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free beach access; parking charges apply after two hours.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A long, attractive and officially managed beach with wildlife, coastal-path access and practical facilities, reduced for weather dependence and the walk from the village centre.

features.fullDescription: The monument comprises an oval enclosure and an unenclosed settlement of prehistoric date, together with a field boundary and cultivation remains of uncertain date, all visible as cropmarks on oblique aerial photographs. The monument lies in arable farmland at around 15m OD. An oval ditched enclosure lies astride a modern field boundary towards the SE end of the scheduled area. The enclosure is aligned NNW-SSE, with an entrance at its NNE end. The enclosure measures 60m long by 44m wide, within ditches about 3m wide. A number of amorphous features, including probable pits, are visible as cropmarks in its interior. To the NW and NNW are at least four sub-circular cropmarks, each measuring between 12m and 14m in diameter, which represent the remains of timber roundhouses. A linear cropmark NW of the enclosure, aligned SW-NE and 185m in length, represents an early field boundary. Cultivation traces are visible to the S of this boundary. The area proposed for scheduling comprises the remains described and an area around them within which related material may be expected to be found. It is irregular in shape, with maximum dimensions of 235m E-W by 155m N-S, as marked in red on the accompanying map extract.

attractionGuide.headline: Two miles of dune-backed East Neuk shore
attractionGuide.intro: Walk the sand and rock pools, watch shore birds and connect with the Fife Coastal Path. Visitor facilities are grouped at the beach car park, about a ten-minute walk from the village.
attractionGuide.parking: Under two hours free, all day £2, disabled daytime parking free; eight overnight motorhome spaces at £10.
attractionGuide.toilets: Public toilet block at the beach car park; an overnight toilet is confirmed by the site manager.
attractionGuide.picnic: Mapped picnic areas and tables beside the beach car park.
attractionGuide.foodNote: Harbour Burger is the currently supported beach food truck; opening reduces in winter.

trails.name: Kingsbarns and Cambo Circuit
trails.summary: A 5.25 km beach, estate and farmland circuit starting at the car park.
trails.difficulty: Coastal and woodland paths, some steps and potentially muddy sections.

thingsToDo.name: Walk Cambo Sands
thingsToDo.summary: Follow the dune-backed shore while avoiding fragile vegetation.

thingsToDo.name: Watch shore birds
thingsToDo.summary: Look for eider, oystercatcher and redshank.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A long, attractive and officially managed beach with wildlife, coastal-path access and practical facilities, reduced for weather dependence and the walk from the village centre.
